title: Soil phase relationships: void ratio, porosity, water content and saturation
examples: What is void ratio in soil?
How do you draw a soil phase diagram?

explain.say: Scoop up a bucket of soil and it is not just soil: it is grains, water and air mixed together. Engineers imagine squeezing each part into its own layer, like the layers in a glass of bubble tea. On the board, one cubic metre of soil, sorted into air, water and solid grains.

draw.text: Soil phase relationships: void ratio, porosity, water content and saturation

explain.say: Start at the bottom: the solid grains, zero point six cubic metres. With a specific gravity of two point six five, typical for quartz sand, they weigh one thousand five hundred and ninety kilograms. Everything else is voids, the spaces between grains: zero point four cubic metres. What fills those voids?

Water and air! Now the key ratios. Void ratio e is voids over solids: zero point four over zero point six, about zero point six seven. Porosity n is voids over the total: zero point four. Degree of saturation S is water over voids: zero point two five over zero point four, sixty two and a half percent.

Water content w, which you measure in the lab by oven drying, is mass of water over mass of solids: two hundred and fifty over fifteen ninety, about fifteen point seven percent. The whole cubic metre weighs eighteen hundred and forty kilograms. If you compacted this soil with a roller, which layer would shrink?

The air layer! Compaction squeezes out air, not grains or water. And one link ties it all together: S times e equals w times G s. Check it: zero point six two five times zero point six seven, and zero point one five seven times two point six five, both give about zero point four two. Brilliant! Use it to check every lab sheet.

faq.a: Void ratio e is the volume of voids divided by the volume of solids. Here 0.4 over 0.6 gives about 0.67; it can be more than 1 for soft clays.

faq.q: What is the difference between void ratio and porosity?
faq.a: Void ratio compares voids with solids, porosity compares voids with the total volume. They are linked by n = e / (1 + e), so porosity is always below 1.
Degree of saturation S is the volume of water divided by the volume of voids. Dry soil has S of 0, fully saturated soil S of 100 percent; here it is 62.5 percent.
Weigh a wet sample, dry it in an oven at about 105 to 110 degrees Celsius for a day, and weigh it again. Water content is the mass of water lost divided by the dry mass.
It links the four main ratios: saturation times void ratio equals water content times specific gravity. Knowing any three gives the fourth, and it is a handy check on lab results.

facts: Porosity and void ratio are linked by n = e/(1 + e).
Most mineral soil grains have a specific gravity between about 2.6 and 2.8.

quiz.say: A soil has a void ratio of 1. What is its porosity, using n equals e over 1 plus e?
quiz.show: A soil has void ratio e = 1.0. Its porosity n = e/(1 + e) is…

wrong.1: That is the void ratio itself, not the porosity.
wrong.2: Porosity can never be more than 1.

quiz.say: A fully saturated soil has a water content of 20 percent and a specific gravity of 2.7. What is its void ratio?
quiz.show: A saturated soil (S = 1) has w = 20% and Gs = 2.7. Void ratio?

wrong.1: That is the water content, not the void ratio.
wrong.2: That is the specific gravity; multiply it by w.
